newsitem.title: UK: Camelot loses again over bid to ban numbers game.
newsitem.headline: Camelot loses again over bid to ban numbers game.

text.p: UK national lottery operator Camelot lost out again on Monday in a legal battle over a numbers game run by UK bookmakers.
Camelot failed in a bid to secure a judicial review of the Director of Public Prosecution's refusal to take action against the bookmakers' "49s" game.
Bookmakers Coral, William Hill and Ladbroke launched the daily numbers game in December to help offset the impact of the national lottery on their business.

Players of the 49's game can bet on between one and five numbers in a daily draw, odds ranging from 11/2 on picking one number to 99,999/1 for all five. The draw is shown in betting shops nationwide on a televised feed.
Camelot argues that the game is an illegal lottery. But Monday's ruling by two of Britain's most senior judges was the second time its call for a judicial review has been rejected.
The lottery operator now has the option of bringing a private prosecution in a bid to have 49's outlawed.
"We are obviously disappointed. We are still none the wiser as to the legality of this game," said a Camelot spokeswoman.
She said the company was reviewing its position in the light of Monday's ruling.

49's Limited welcomed the decision and said they hoped Camelot would now let the matter rest. "We have always been confident of the legality of 49's, a view endorsed by the DPP and the Crown Prosecution Service," the company said in a statement.
"49's is fixed odds betting offered by bookmakers, it is quite distinct in law from a lottery or gaming or pool betting and poses no threat to the national lottery or to the income to good causes."
The bookmakers have been lobbying for the right to take side bets on the national lottery but the government has so far resisted their calls.
Competition from the national lottery has intensified following the launch two months ago of a second weekly draw.

Bookmakers point out that the independent Henley Centre has forecast that the midweek draw will cut their turnover by 3.2 percent annually. The betting industry estimates that 49's will generate jst over three percent of betting turnover and argue it is helping to keep shops open and save jobs. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
